questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
1. academic opportunities
2. international environment
3. possible to get to without an airplane

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to find courses and keep a hold of all of the details with mobility online, host university application requirements and requirements from my own university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a personal meeting with an exchange coordinator that assisted me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: it was quit difficult. I recommend contacting the university if you don't have any housing upon arrival and searching for people going on exchange and renting their room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it can be difficult to find.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I needed a language test to get specific courses, which was a bit much.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I followed the registration proces described on their website. We had to fill out a system including uploading courses, grades etc. I furthermore had to take an English language test.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinators were very available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i was quit confused before getting there, as wasn't eligible for all the courses I wanted to take. However, when I got to Amsterdam it was a lot easier to get an overview of the courses and change courses. Also I took some courses even though I initially wasn't eligible.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't stress too much about not getting the courses immediately. There are different application rounds.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the course level was appropriate, high but not too high. They had progressive climate courses which was nice!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: 2 hours lectures and seminars instead of many hours at UCPH. There was quit a lot of monitoring/examination compared to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Degrowth
Rethinking sustainable societies: new perspectives
political economy of global food chains
Environment and international sustainable development
Cities facing climate change: an urban political ecology approach

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Degrowth: very hard to find a course elsewhere and very relevant to learn about this. 
political economy of global food chains: good introduction to global political economy 
environment and international sustainable development: very nice course, interesting and well structured. Also from a political ecology perspective!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
you spend more money on clubs, cinemas, cafes, museums etc. because you are on exchange and want to experience the city.... 
deposit as well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: housing is expensive. I found it very cheaply, but some people spend more than 1000 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very nice! they had a lot of creative and sport offers and even their own bouldering gym!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: honestly most activities. They have a space called crea where they have dance, painting, photography etc. and a huge sport center.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
bouldering and a course at crea! going to the cinema. They have cineville in amsterdam: unlimited cinema for 20 euros per month. a lot of nice and cute cinemas that also play non-mainstream movies. 
Kriterion! a cute student led bar/cafe and cinema right next to uni with cheap coffee. 
Visit squatting places and go to their community dinners etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wereld museum about the colonial past (and present) of the Netherlands! markets, throwing dinners etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: quit easy. Amsterdam is very international, so a lot of people speak English and a lot of different cultures meet.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk to people in your classes and ask if they want to grab a beer. My experience was that everyone was quit open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not really any I think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: all of the nice markets, being open, the squatting culture and international environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be aware that there Is a lot of school, get a bike, go to the introduction week to meet people when you arrive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you want to deregister from a course you can do it yourself in Glass. However, the deadline is 14 days after the course begins.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting a lot of nice people and exploring the city with them!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: balancing not spending too much time at school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
